GHSA-36xv-jgw5-4q75.title: @nestjs/core Improperly Neutralizes Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Compon
GHSA-36xv-jgw5-4q75.why: CVE-2026-35515. Read the advisory on 24.09.2026 rather than reasoning from the title, and the vector is narrower and more checkable than the earlier note here said. The flaw is in SseStream._transform(): \r and \n from message.type and message.id are interpolated into the Server-Sent Events text protocol unsanitised, which lets an attacker spoof an event type or corrupt reconnection state. GitHub's advisory states the precondition outright: 'Requires the developer to map user-influenced data to the type or id fields of SSE messages. Direct HTTP request input does not reach these fields without developer code bridging the gap.' We ship no SSE at all - grepped apps/api/src on 24.09.2026: zero @Sse decorators, zero 'text/event-stream', zero Observable<MessageEvent>. There is no endpoint for this to reach. ⚠️ REVISIT THE DAY AN SSE ENDPOINT IS ADDED: on that day this stops being unreachable and the upgrade becomes a blocker rather than a deferral. The previous wording ('our responses are JSON built from typed values') was true but would have let somebody add SSE tomorrow and still believe they were covered. On the fix: it landed in 11.1.18, NOT only in 12.x as the earlier note implied - but we are on 10.4.22, so any fix is still a major for us. Dependabot PR #29 offers 12.1.0, published 23.09.2026, which is two majors and one day old; dependabot.yml sets semver-major-days: 30 and ignores @nestjs/* majors for version updates, and a security update bypasses both by design. The wait rule governs here because the security exception exists for fixes we need, and this is not one.
